effect_estimate.comment: Exact 95% CIs and p-values are plotted graphically in Fig. 8 (PDF p. 7) and reported in Supplementary Tables 5-6 rather than printed numerically in the main text.
effect_estimate.value: Across 31,383 Census block groups in 9 U.S. states, unincorporated communities have nearly 30% of land area unsewered on average compared to 11% in incorporated communities (median unsewered area: 15% in Islands, 3.7% in Fringes, 3.1% in Outlying, and ~0% in incorporated block groups; in the highest poverty tercile >=20.5%, median unsewered area is 19.0% in Islands and 11.8% in Outlying vs. 4.5% in Fringes and 0% in incorporated block groups). In multilevel negative binomial GLM regressions with county and state random effects (relative to incorporated block groups), unincorporated status among high-poverty block groups (>=20% below Federal poverty line) is associated with an incidence rate ratio (IRR) of 3.54 for unsewered land area and IRR = 17.8 for land area unserved by centralized drinking water, whereas among block groups without high poverty, unincorporated status is associated with IRR = 1.48 for unsewered area. Without poverty interactions, Island unincorporated block groups have the largest IRR for unsewered area (IRR = 2.47) and Outlying unincorporated block groups have the largest IRR for area unserved by centralized water (IRR = 5.53); with high-poverty interactions, both Island and Outlying high-poverty block groups exceed IRR = 4.0 for unsewered area (vs. IRR = 0.91 for Outlying block groups without high poverty).
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 5-8, Results (Summary statistics, Regression results, Fig. 6-8) & Discussion

mechanism_certainty.comment: Cross-sectional spatial regression design (JBI ceiling of 2). Assigned 1 because the study empirically documents statistical and spatial associations between municipal incorporation status / buffer proximity to city boundaries (1.6 km proxy for extraterritorial jurisdiction) and utility service area coverage, while legal-administrative mechanisms such as selective annexation (underbounding), extraterritorial planning restrictions, and funding eligibility barriers are discussed contextually rather than directly observed at the administrative decision level.

outcome_flags.comment: Measures block-group proportion of land area served/unserved by centralized community water systems (CWS) and publicly-owned treatment works (POTW) sewer service areas, including parcel-level centralized water and sewer connections in Florida. Affordability and connection fees are discussed only in policy recommendations (PDF p. 9), not empirically measured.
